title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + compaction heuristics v21 (reduce fragmentation, async spill/paging)
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Improve KV cache memory utilization and reduce spillover by adding adaptive compaction, fragmentation-aware eviction scoring, and async CPU spill/prefetch. Expected throughput +8-12% on tail-heavy workloads and 25-40% reduction in runtime spill events.
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and coarse eviction scoring have been a persistent source of increased host spillover (paging to host/SSD) and unpredictable latency on long-running chats. This PR implements a set of interlocking runtime improvements: 1) an adaptive compaction pass that opportunistically coalesces fragmented free blocks within a shard to reduce allocation failures, 2) a fragmentation-aware eviction scorer that factors in allocation span and block fragmentation in addition to recency/weight, 3) a low-latency async spill/paging pipeline that moves cold KV pages to host memory (and SSD as fallback) with prioritized prefetch for predicted next-step requests, and 4) scheduler-level backpressure heuristics to prefer hot-session pinning over global eviction during short bursts. Implementation notes: - New allocator module changes in src/runtime/kv_cache/allocator.cpp/h that expose compaction hooks and fragmentation metrics. Compaction is bounded by a per-shard CPU budget (configurable) and runs during idle ticks or when free space drops below threshold. - Eviction scoring updated in src/runtime/kv_cache/evict_policy.cpp: score = alpha*LRU + beta*size_penalty + gamma*fragmentation_penalty + delta*pinned_penalty. Default weights tuned from perf-canary runs. - Async spill pipeline in src/runtime/kv_cache/spill_async.cpp with a small worker pool, scatter/gather prefetch, and backoff on high IO pressure. Molecule-level metadata persisted to spill index for fast rehydration. - Scheduler changes to scheduler.cpp to prefer serving cached hot sessions (pin hint) and delay bulk eviction until compaction completes. - Extensive tracing, new metrics (kv.compaction.runs, kv.fragmentation.percentile, kv.spill.events, kv.async_prefetch.latency) and dashboards updated. - Tests: unit tests for allocator/compaction, integration perf harness additions, and a new stress test (tests/kv_cache/fragmentation_stress.cc). Backwards compatibility: feature gated by runtime flag kv.cache.adaptive_compaction=true and spill/paging disabled by default on Private installs. Docs: brief doc added to docs/operational/kv-cache.md describing flags and recommended tuning. Perf summary: - Simulated long-chat workload (median sequence 1.6k tokens): 9-12% higher steady throughput on A100 pools when compaction budget=5% CPU and eviction weights tuned. - Production perf-canary (20% traffic): observed 28% reduction in host spill events and 18% lower P95 latency during peak sustained load. - Storage IO: async spill reduced synchronous IO stalls by ~40% in canary. Risk and rollout: changes are moderately invasive to allocator path; rollout plan is to enable adaptive compaction in canary -> staged rollout in Dedicated -> enable for Hosted with conservative defaults. Linked Linear tickets ENG-4621 (kv-cache fragmentation investigation) and ENG-4788 (reduce spillover on long chats).
